author: JoLan_07
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – 1/10
This game has so many things worth criticizing that giving it a 10/10 feels just as ridiculous as giving it a 1/10. So, my initial review score will be exactly that: 1/10. That doesn’t mean my review is invalid, but I need to make several things absolutely clear.
1. No First-Person Mode. There is no first-person mode, and somehow none of the major critics seem to mention this. I guess that’s still a 10/10, right? They removed a feature that was already available in GTA V, a game originally released on PS3, and Red Dead Redemption 2, which came out on PS4. Yet somehow, GTA VI can’t have it? Seriously?
2. An Extremely Boring Protagonist
The protagonist is incredibly boring and has absolutely zero charisma. And apparently, I CAN’T CHEAT! This is the most anticipated game in 13 years, a game where you can supposedly build a relationship, yet I’m not even allowed to cheat on a woman who clearly isn’t mentally stable? That’s ridiculous. The lack of such a basic choice in a game that supposedly offers so much freedom is just stupid.
3. Jason’s Voice Acting
Jason’s voice acting is terrible. His delivery is so dull and lifeless that his dialogue genuinely makes me sleepy. Listening to him is a chore rather than an enjoyable part of the experience.
4. The Downgrade, Bugs, and the Media’s Double Standards (Cyberpunk) 
For what is supposed to be the most ambitious video game ever made, GTA VI is honestly a massive disappointment so far. The downgrade is noticeable, and don’t even get me started on all the glitches and bugs. But apparently, it’s still a 10/10 for the gaming press, right? What a **** we actually want games to improve, we can’t just stay silent and hand out perfect scores. Sometimes you have to be the black sheep and give an honest review, even if everyone disagrees with you. I’d rather be the black sheep than another mindless sheep blindly following the herd.
5. Ridiculous and Inconsistent Endings
Some of the endings are just ridiculous and completely inconsistent with the expectations many players have for the story. Sure, certain endings might work for a small minority of players, but that doesn’t mean the majority will find them satisfying. A game’s ending should feel earned, coherent, and consistent with the characters and the story. Not every ending deserves praise just because it’s different or unexpected.
Final thoughts: 1/10. A game doesn’t deserve a perfect score simply because it took years to make, has an enormous budget, or carries the weight of an iconic franchise. Judge the game for what it actually delivers, not for the expectations surrounding it.
